text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Swedish authorities have issued such a complicated application form for state housing allowances for individuals that more than 70 percent of forms received by authorities had to be returned to applicants for addition information.
- Domestic private consumption is picking up with the clothing sector boosting sales in fixed prices by up to 9.5 percent in December. Other retailers show similar figures.

- U.K. bus group Stagecoach plans staff cuts and cost cutting on the purchasing side of its Swedish subsidiary Swebus that will lead to more departures and lower ticket prices for Swebus passengers, says Brian Souter, head of Stagecoach.
- Every fourth Swede is against Sweden joining Europe's Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), according to a survey by pollster Skop.
- Swedish automotive group AB Volvo increased car sales in Japan by 17 percent to 24,037 cars in 1996. The company expects to sell 25,000 cars in Japan this year.
- Sweden's competition authority accuses the post office of using political favours and manipulating data in its attempt to fight off competition.

- British bus group Stagecoach's acquisition of Swedish bus company Swebus may lead to more competition on the public transportation market. Stagecoach says it is planning to launch a programme in Sweden which will target low-income groups.

- International electrical engineering group ABB has two orders in the pipeline worth around five billion crowns. One is for a direct power cable link between Sweden and Poland and the other is for a power and desalination plan in Bahrain.
